subject.title: Feature Request: Support message recall/edit events to cancel running tasks

question: Should OpenClaw define a shared source-message lifecycle contract for channel edit/delete/recall events, or continue landing channel-specific cancellation/edit behavior without a shared core/plugin contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects plugin API boundaries, session state, channel delivery, and user-visible cancellation defaults across multiple transports.

options.title: Define Shared Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Add a narrow source-message lifecycle contract and require channel plugins to map native edit/delete/recall events into it before cancelling or superseding runs.

options.title: Land Channel Slices Only
options.body: Review and land proof-positive channel-specific PRs independently while accepting duplicated semantics until a repeated pattern forces a shared contract.

options.title: Defer Until One Channel Lands
options.body: Keep the umbrella open but wait for a live-proven channel implementation to establish the minimum viable behavior before standardizing the API.

recommendation.title: Define Shared Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow source-message lifecycle contract and require channel plugins to map native edit/delete/recall events into it before cancelling or superseding runs.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across chat abort semantics and the shared channel/inbound architecture that the decision must fit.
